schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    USER_ID INT,
    SESSION_ID INT,
    ACTIVITY_DATE DATE,
    ACTIVITY_TYPE ENUM('OPEN_SESSION', 'END_SESSION', 'SCROLL_DOWN', 'SEND_MESSAGE'),
    CHECK (ACTIVITY_TYPE IN ('OPEN_SESSION', 'END_SESSION', 'SCROLL_DOWN', 'SEND_MESSAGE'))
);
q1: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27' GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q2: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE DATEDIFF(ACTIVITY_DATE,'2019-07-27')<29 AND DATEDIFF(ACTIVITY_DATE,'2019-07-27')>-30 GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27' GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE DATEDIFF(ACTIVITY_DATE,'2019-07-27')<29 AND DATEDIFF(ACTIVITY_DATE,'2019-07-27')>-30 GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTIVITY (USER_ID, SESSION_ID, ACTIVITY_DATE, ACTIVITY_TYPE) VALUES (1, 1, '2019-07-27', 'OPEN_SESSION');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 uses a BETWEEN clause to select activity dates between '2019-06-28' and '2019-07-27', inclusive. Q2 uses DATEDIFF to select activity dates that are less than 29 days before '2019-07-27' and more than 30 days before '2019-07-27'. This range is not equivalent to the one in Q1. Specifically, Q2's range includes dates starting from '2019-06-28' to '2019-07-27', but it also excludes the end date '2019-07-27'.
counterexample_dsp: Create a test database where there is one activity record on '2019-07-27'. Q1 will count it, but Q2 will not because DATEDIFF('2019-07-27', '2019-07-27') = 0 which is not < 29 and not > -30.
